claims.hypothesis: The outburst of HOPS 383 has left a chemical signature in the envelope (CO evaporation destroying N2H+ and forming HCO+)

claims.finding: The N2H+ depression is consistent with CO evaporation after the outburst, though of marginal significance

evidence.quote: This reflects the underlying chemistry where CO evaporating close to the protostar destroys N$_2$H$^+$ while forming HCO$^+$.
although of marginal significance, this morphology suggests that this molecule is being destroyed by reactions with the evaporating CO molecules, forming HCO$^+$.

evidence.quote: The models including VLA 8 mm data indicate that the disk mass could be up to a factor of 10 larger due to lower dust opacity at longer wavelengths.
In addition, the VLA data that we used for modeling contains a free-free contribution as well, which can further increase the estimate the disk mass.

claims.hypothesis: Gravitational instability is a viable mechanism for the HOPS 383 outburst
claims.experiment: Toomre Q from flux-derived masses and from model surface density and temperature profiles, with temperatures scaled back to the pre-outburst luminosity
claims.result: Q = 1.67 (0.043 Msun) and 0.87 (0.082 Msun) at 0.5 Msun; ALMA-only model disks stable but near Q=1, ALMA+VLA models unstable near the critical radius
claims.finding: Disk appears to have sufficient mass for GI to be a very plausible outburst mechanism, but instability is not confirmed

evidence.quote: Thus, while we cannot absolutely confirm that the disk is or was unstable, the disk appears to have sufficient mass to make gravitational instability a very plausible outburst mechanism for HOPS 383.

claims.hypothesis: Outflow knots record past accretion bursts
claims.experiment: Dynamical timescale of knots from the ALMA 12CO cube and spacing of knots in the SMA maps
claims.result: Closest knot ~215 yr old; knots spaced ~1400 yr apart
claims.finding: The closest knot predates the 2006 burst; knot spacing is consistent with the Orion burst rate of Fischer et al. 2019, if knots and bursts are one-to-one

evidence.quote: However, if there is a one-to-one relationship between accretion bursts and outflow knots, there could have been past outbursts in HOPS 383.

why_this_data.value: ALMA masses are emphasised because the appropriate 9 mm dust opacity for the VLA data is uncertain

evidence.quote: We focus on the ALMA masses because the appropriate dust opacity at 9 mm for the VLA observations is uncertain.

why_this_method.value: Both truncated and exponentially tapered disks are modeled because it is unclear which better reflects the disk structure

evidence.quote: We model two different types of disks as it is unclear which type of disk better reflects the underlying protostellar disk structure.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Tapered models give less reliable disk radii than truncated models, so the truncated radii are favored

evidence.quote: For this reason, we favor the truncated models values of disk radius.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: N2H+ structure may reflect cumulative effects of multiple bursts rather than only the latest one

evidence.quote: the observed structure of N$_2$H$^+$ could be a chemical feature that may represent the cumulative effect of multiple outbursts, rather than the latest one.

how_they_decided_enough.value: Fits stopped when best-fit values stay constant for ~150-200 steps

evidence.quote: the best fit values of the parameters remain more or less constant for $\sim$ 150 - 200 steps.

limitations_admitted.value: Analytic ALMA disk masses are lower limits if the 0.87 mm emission is optically thick

evidence.quote: The dust emission may not be optically thin at 0.87 mm for all radii, thus, the disk masses are likely lower limits for their respective temperatures.

limitations_admitted.value: VLA visibility fits omit the free-free contribution; models cannot fit VLA visibilities without worsening the SED fit

evidence.quote: Our models are not able to fully reproduce the visibilities from the VLA, without sacrificing the fit for the SED.
The fitting to the visibility data from the VLA also does not account for a contribution from the free-free emission

limitations_admitted.value: Envelope properties are poorly constrained for lack of short baselines

evidence.quote: While we model the envelopes, their properties are expected to be poorly constrained due to the lack of short baseline data.

limitations_admitted.value: SMA C18O is contaminated by a foreground cloud

evidence.quote: our C$^{18}$O data cube is contaminated by a foreground cloud that is also emitting at a similar velocity range

referee_caveats_inferred: The ALMA-based results rest on a single 54 s observation; self-calibration and imaging parameters (clean mask, threshold, cell, image size) are not given
Disk mass depends on assumed opacity, beta, temperature and the 100:1 gas-to-dust ratio; 0.082 vs 0.043 Msun spans a factor of two
The Toomre Q inference uses an assumed 0.5 Msun protostar mass and an unstated radius; pre-outburst luminosity is 0.2 Lsun in some places and 0.5 Lsun in others

Internal inconsistencies: VLA 9 mm flux given as 411 +/- 17 uJy (Results) and 411 +/- 1.7 uJy (Disk Mass); conclusions quote model disk mass 0.1 Msun/radius ~67 au and 0.065 Msun/~40 au versus Table 2 values of 0.026/0.020 Msun and 65/38 au
N2H+ double-peaked structure is of marginal significance (5-7 sigma peak S/N) and chemistry conclusions come from SMA data, not ALMA
Free-free is not modeled in the ALMA+VLA visibility fits, so the factor-of-10 mass increase is partly spurious by the authors' own estimate

missing_for_reproduction: Self-calibration and clean settings for the ALMA continuum
SED photometry table used in the model fits
MCMC priors, walker/step counts, visibility binning and pdspy version
Coordinates and exact distance adoption for HOPS 383
Reduced ALMA visibilities (manually calibrated by the ARC node) are not stated to be released
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Small: one ALMA Band 7 project (2015.1.00041.S), two short execution blocks, a few GB to tens of GB of raw data
reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA project code, CASA version, robust, flux calibrators and key analytic formulae with numeric results are given, so the continuum flux, size and analytic disk mass are reproducible; the radiative transfer modeling lacks priors, SED data and self-calibration detail, and the calibration was done manually.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The ALMA project code is printed and the data come from the VANDAM survey; the continuum flux, Gaussian size, inclination and analytic disk masses are numeric and redoable, though the full RT model fit is not completely specified.
